paragraphs: Deep in a quiet forest, beside a river, lived a yogi who spent his days meditating, studying and practising hard disciplines. He was famous for his learning. A poor, unlettered cowherd grazed his cattle in the same forest, and day after day he watched the yogi sitting for hours in meditation. Slowly he grew curious.

One day he gathered his courage and asked the yogi to teach him how to reach God. The yogi brushed him off: how could a simple cowherd ever understand God? He should go home and look after his cows. But a real longing had awakened in the man. He came back and asked again, and was turned away again. Still he could not eat or sleep. He had to know.

When he came a third time, the yogi decided to get rid of him with a quick answer. The cowherd asked what God looked like. The yogi told him God was just like the big bull in his herd. That bull was God.

The cowherd believed every word. He went home and began to worship the bull day and night. He fetched it the freshest grass, slept beside it, lit a lamp for it, sat with it and followed it everywhere. Months and years went by, and his whole heart was poured into that bull.

Then one day he heard a voice that seemed to come from the bull, calling him 'my son'. Bulls can't talk, he thought. When the voice came again, he understood: it was rising from his own heart. God was within him, always with him.

Later he went to see the yogi. The yogi, for all his years of study and austerity, saw the cowherd's face shining with a heavenly light and asked where this had come from. The cowherd said the yogi himself had given it to him. The yogi protested that he had only been joking. But the cowherd had taken it seriously, and since God is everywhere, he had found Him through the bull. Swamiji explained that the bull was a pratika, a symbol. Intense love can draw everything out of us, because everything is already within; outward forms of worship simply awaken the Lord inside.
learn: Sincerity can matter more than sophistication. Whatever starting point you have, a symbol, a practice or a simple goal, steady wholehearted effort can unlock what is already inside you. And never look down on someone's sincere question.
